questions.stem:
(a) Draw, in words, the structure of an NPN transistor and name its terminals. [3 marks]
(b) Describe how an analogue multimeter on the ohms range can be used to test an NPN transistor. [6 marks]
(c) Compare the common emitter, common base and common collector configurations in terms of input impedance, output impedance and voltage gain. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) thin P-type base sandwiched between N-type emitter and N-type collector; terminals emitter, base, collector
2 marks: (b) base-emitter junction: low resistance one way, high reversed (like a diode)
2 marks: (b) base-collector junction: low resistance one way, high reversed
2 marks: (b) collector-emitter: high resistance both ways; low in both directions indicates short
2 marks: (c) CE: medium input impedance, medium-high output, high voltage gain
2 marks: (c) CB: low input impedance, high output, high voltage gain
2 marks: (c) CC: high input impedance, low output, voltage gain about 1
questions.explanation: NPN: thin P base between N emitter and collector. Test each junction as a diode; C-E should be high both ways. CE gives high gain; CB low input impedance; CC high input, low output, unity gain.

questions.stem:
(a) Name, in order, the blocks of a regulated d.c. power supply. [4 marks]
(b) A 230 V mains transformer has 1150 primary turns and 60 secondary turns and feeds a bridge rectifier. Calculate (i) the secondary r.m.s. voltage, (ii) the peak voltage, (iii) the ripple frequency on 50 Hz mains. [6 marks]
(c) Explain how a reservoir capacitor smooths the output. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: (a) transformer, rectifier, filter (smoothing), regulator (stabiliser) (1 each)
2 marks: (b)(i) Vs = 230 x 60/1150 = 12 V
2 marks: (b)(ii) peak = 12 x 1.414 = 17 V
2 marks: (b)(iii) ripple = 2 x 50 = 100 Hz
3 marks: (c) capacitor charges to peak when rectifier output rises
2 marks: (c) discharges slowly into the load between peaks, filling the gaps and reducing ripple
questions.explanation: Blocks: transformer, rectifier, filter, regulator. Vs = 12 V, peak 17 V, ripple 100 Hz. Capacitor charges at peaks and supplies the load between them.

questions.stem:
(a) Define modulation and state two reasons why it is necessary. [5 marks]
(b) Distinguish between amplitude modulation and frequency modulation. [4 marks]
(c) An AM carrier of 20 V amplitude is modulated so that the envelope varies between 30 V and 10 V. Calculate the modulation index. [3 marks]
(d) State three advantages of FM over AM. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) modulation: varying a property of a high-frequency carrier in step with the information signal
4 marks: (a) reasons any two: practical antenna size, allows many stations by frequency division, long-distance propagation (2 each)
2 marks: (b) AM: amplitude of carrier varies, frequency constant
2 marks: (b) FM: frequency of carrier varies, amplitude constant
3 marks: (c) m = (30 - 10)/(30 + 10) = 0.5
3 marks: (d) any three: less noise, better fidelity, constant amplitude so efficient transmitter, capture effect (1 each)
questions.explanation: Modulation impresses information on a carrier, enabling small antennas and multiple stations. AM varies amplitude; FM varies frequency. m = 20/40 = 0.5. FM has less noise and better fidelity.

questions.topic: Principles of Operation of Colour Television Receiver
questions.stem:
(a) Name the three primary colours used in colour television. [3 marks]
(b) Write the luminance equation for the PAL system. [3 marks]
(c) State the function of each of the following stages of a colour TV receiver: (i) tuner, (ii) video IF amplifier, (iii) chroma decoder. [6 marks]
(d) Name the three colour television standards. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) red, green, blue
3 marks: (b) Y = 0.30R + 0.59G + 0.11B
2 marks: (c)(i) tuner selects the channel and converts it to IF
2 marks: (c)(ii) video IF amplifies the IF signal and provides selectivity
2 marks: (c)(iii) chroma decoder recovers colour difference signals from the chrominance signal
3 marks: (d) PAL, NTSC, SECAM
questions.explanation: Primaries R, G, B; Y = 0.30R + 0.59G + 0.11B. Tuner selects channel, IF amplifies, chroma decoder recovers colour difference signals. Standards PAL, NTSC, SECAM.

questions.topic: Fault Finding and Repairs in Radio Receiver
questions.stem:
(a) Explain the logical steps of fault-finding in a radio receiver. [6 marks]
(b) A transistor radio is completely dead. State five checks you would carry out. [5 marks]
(c) Explain what is meant by alignment of a radio receiver and name two instruments used. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
6 marks: (a) gather symptoms from customer; visual inspection; check power supply; signal injection/tracing stage by stage from speaker back to aerial; measure voltages; replace faulty component and test (1 each)
5 marks: (b) battery/power supply, on/off switch and volume control, fuse/power cable, loudspeaker continuity, supply rail voltages and output transistors (1 each)
2 marks: (c) alignment: adjusting tuned circuits (IF transformers, oscillator and RF trimmers) for maximum output at correct frequencies
2 marks: (c) signal generator and output meter/oscilloscope/frequency counter (1 each)
questions.explanation: Fault-finding: symptoms, inspection, power checks, signal injection/tracing, voltage measurement, repair and test. Dead set: power, switch, fuse, speaker, rails. Alignment tunes IF/RF/oscillator circuits using a signal generator and output meter.

questions.stem:
(a) Name four business records a radio and TV repair shop should keep and state the use of each. [8 marks]
(b) State three sources of capital for starting the business. [3 marks]
(c) State four qualities of good customer relations. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
8 marks: (a) any four with use: repair order form (records customer item and fault), inventory sheet (tracks stock of parts), ledger (records transactions), cash book (receipts and payments), receipts/invoices (proof of payment) (2 each)
3 marks: (b) any three: personal savings, bank loan, credit union/cooperative, family and friends, government grants (1 each)
4 marks: (c) any four: neat appearance, politeness, honesty, keeping promised dates, telephone courtesy, listening to complaints (1 each)
questions.explanation: Records: repair order forms, inventory sheets, ledger, cash book, receipts. Capital: savings, banks, cooperatives, family. Good relations: neatness, politeness, honesty, punctuality, courtesy.
